chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the leftover water of a menstruating woman.

He said: “Wudu (ablution) may be performed from it; and perform wudu (ablution) from the leftover water of a junub when she is trustworthy, and she washes her hand before putting it into the vessel. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform ghusl with ʿĀʾishah from one vessel, and the two of them would perform ghusl together.”

key_terms.الْإِنَاءَ: the vessel or container holding water
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or remainder from which someone has drunk or used
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trusted as clean and careful regarding impurity

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed from the leftover water of a menstruating woman or a junub?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and the use of leftover water touched by a menstruating woman or a junub. It indicates the permissibility of using such water for wudu (ablution), with the condition of cleanliness and trustworthiness, and supports this by citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
